sources.title: Acceptable Refrigerants and their Impacts
readSections: Environmental Impacts of MVAC Refrigerants table
sources.readMethod: Independent actual web open of the official page; author summary not substituted for source reading.
supportedClaims: CFC-12 formerly used in motor-vehicle cooling; HFC-134a used as replacement/refrigerant.
CFC-12 is ozone-depleting; HFC-134a is not and has substantial greenhouse impact.
Benefits, climate, ozone, flammability and health are distinct comparison criteria.
limits: US regulatory statements on the page establish no German permission or deadline.
The packet does not require the displayed GWP numbers or treat an ozone-safe label as overall environmental neutrality.
CFC-12 also has greenhouse impact; A1 is a selected pathway dossier, not an exhaustive hazard inventory.

sources.title: Information on Ozone and Ozone Depletion
readSections: Opening scientific paragraphs on ozone, UV-B and stratospheric conversion
sources.readMethod: Independent actual web open of the official page.
supportedClaims: Certain released chlorine/bromine-containing chemicals reach the stratosphere, where UV converts them into ozone-destroying reactive species.
UV-B exposure can affect people and ecosystems.
limits: This is an accessible scientific summary, not a detailed kinetic derivation.
A1 appropriately states a conditional atmospheric pathway rather than an immediate local UV effect.

sources.publisher: CDC / National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health
sources.title: NIOSH Pocket Guide: Dichlorodifluoromethane
sources.readMethod: Independent actual successful web open of the official page, including the hazard entries. No separate raw HTML fetch was needed or claimed.
supportedClaims: Dizziness, asphyxia, arrhythmia and other acute effects are listed; liquid contact can cause frostbite.
limits: Occupational limits do not establish a safe concentration for the museum case.
No release amount, concentration or actual exposure is established by the case.

sources.title: International Chemical Safety Card 1281: 1,1,1,2-Tetrafluoroethane
sources.readMethod: Independent actual web open of the official card.
supportedClaims: HFC-134a identity and C2H2F4 formula, containing no chlorine.
High local inhalation exposure can have central nervous system/cardiovascular effects.
Loss of containment can rapidly produce harmful gas concentrations; evaporating liquid can cause frostbite.
limits: The card is dated and supports stable identity/acute-hazard statements, not current law or a complete comparative lifecycle assessment.
No local exposure level is calculable from B.
